newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar shrugs off weak GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar shrugs off weak GDP data.

text.p: The Singapore dollar remained relatively resilient on Wednesday, tracking the U.S. dollar's moves in a narrow range, despite news of weak third quarter domestic growth and the government's downward revision of its 1996 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) forecast.

"The market chose not to react last night when the news came out. Then when the dollar/majors dropped off 80-100 points, dollar/Sing moved about 10-15 points to 1.4085/90," said a Japanese bank dealer.

He said dollar/Sing had continued to move in line with the dollar/majors on Wednesday, rising above the 1.41 level when the U.S. dollar shot above 114.60 yen on euphoria over President Bill Clinton's re-election and the prospect of a continued Republican majority in Congress.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4090/97 to the U.S. dollar after the Asian close against its opening 1.4084/1.4094.
Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong announced late on Tuesday that third quarter growth was 3.2 percent, down sharply from the second quarter's 7.5 percent.
He also said the government expected 1996 GDP to be around six percent against a previous forecast of 7.0-8.0 percent.
"The figures had been largely discounted...so I don't see it as having any material impact," said a U.S. bank dealer.
"The GDP growth in the third quarter was on the higher end of market expectations," said Andy Tan, economist at MMS International.

The Japanese bank dealer echoed Tan's view, adding that the market had expected the full year GDP forecast to be revised down to 6.0-6.5 percent after growth in the second quarter fell to 7.5 percent against 11.4 percent in the first quarter.
He said the Singapore dollar was likely to trade in a 1.4060-1.4120 range against the U.S. dollar over the next week.
